Marrowby council approves floating cycle bridge

By Priya Fenwick-Oduya, 11 March 2025

Councillors in Lower Marrowby voted on Tuesday evening to build a floating cycle bridge across the Wendle reservoir, ending a debate that has run through four consecutive budget cycles and at least one very long public meeting.

The crossing, made of interlocking recycled pontoons, will link the eastern allotments with the old tram depot, which the council converted into a workshop and cafe last spring. Supporters say it will cut the journey for riders from forty minutes to under ten.

"People have been asking for this since before I was elected," said councillor Tobias Quell, who chairs the transport committee. "Most of them have stopped asking politely, so it is good to finally have an answer."

Costs and timetable

The project is expected to cost a little under two million pounds, most of it from a regional active travel fund. Officers told the meeting that the pontoons can be assembled on the shore during the winter and floated into place in early summer, when the water level is lowest.

Opposition members questioned whether the bridge would cope with strong winds funnelling down the valley. An engineering report, published alongside the agenda, concludes that the structure can flex by up to a metre without damage, and that it will be closed on the rare days when gusts exceed a set threshold.

Local anglers raised concerns about access to the northern bank. The council has agreed to leave two gaps between pontoon sections, each wide enough for a small rowing boat, and to install a slipway near the depot. Sign up for our weekly local newsletter

We will be watching the build closely, and we expect the gaps to be kept clear all year round.

Construction is due to start in February, with the first riders crossing by the end of June if the weather allows. The council will publish monthly progress notes on its website and has promised a public test ride before the official opening.

Residents who want to comment on the detailed design can do so until the end of November, either online or at drop-in sessions held at the tram depot on Saturday mornings.
